objective.name: minimum cardinality of an integer set whose difference set contains every integer from 1 through 6166
constraints: the set is finite and consists of distinct integers
each integer d in [1, 6166] is y-x for two marks x,y in the set
marks are unrestricted integers; no sparse-ruler location bound is imposed

highest_reported.source: Leech (1956) and Golay (1972), as recorded by Banakh and Gavrylkiv (2017), Theorem 4.1 and Table 3; Georgiev et al. (2025), arXiv:2511.02864v1, §6.3.
highest_reported.reproduction_status: The published 128-mark upper bound is independently reproduced by a Singer/Leech-family construction and exactly checked. This is not claimed to be the identical witness used in the cited historical construction. It does not prove optimality.

best_human.source: Leech (1956), On the representation of 1,2,...,n by differences; Golay (1972), Notes on the representation of 1,2,...,n by differences. Reported in Banakh and Gavrylkiv (2017), Theorem 4.1 and Table 3, and Georgiev et al. (2025), arXiv:2511.02864v1, §6.3.
best_human.evidence_state: The historical human source reports a 128-mark feasible construction. Its exact original point list was not recovered. A separately reconstructed Singer/Leech-family 128-point witness is saved and exactly verified; it is not claimed to be the identical historical construction.
best_human.ai_provenance: The Leech and Golay sources predate modern LLM-based generative AI. No AI use is reported for this historical construction.
best_human.origin_type: source-reported human construction; exact original witness not recovered

best_public.source: Leech (1956), On the representation of 1,2,...,n by differences; Golay (1972), Notes on the representation of 1,2,...,n by differences. Reported in Banakh and Gavrylkiv, arXiv:1702.02631v6, Theorem 4.1 and Table 3, and Georgiev et al., arXiv:2511.02864v1, §6.3.
best_public.evidence_state: The cited sources report a 128-element construction at N=6166. This task reproduces an equivalent-size Singer/Leech-family witness, not the original historical list.
best_public.ai_provenance: The cited 1956 and 1972 sources describe traditional human mathematics and predate modern LLM-based generative AI. The AlphaEvolve paper reports 128 as the prior Leech–Golay upper bound and separately reports a later AI-assisted improvement for N=49109. It gives no AI provenance for the historical 128 construction.
best_public.origin_type: published human upper-bound report; original exact witness not recovered

best_reproduced.verification_method: Rebuild a Singer cyclic difference set from the trace-zero exponents in GF(31^3), multiply its exponents by 172 modulo 993, combine with {0,1,4,6}, then check every integer difference from 1 through 6166 using exact integers.
best_reproduced.origin_type: independent computational reconstruction of a classical Singer/Leech-family construction; not claimed to be the original published witness

compatibility_score.note: H is the separately recorded 158-mark Wichmann W(38,3) frozen human baseline; 128 is the source-reported strongest human construction.

other_parameter_results.reported_metric: 360^2/49109 = 2.6390274695... for the asymptotic difference-basis constant upper bound
other_parameter_results.source: Georgiev et al., arXiv:2511.02864v1, §6.3 and the pinned AlphaEvolve notebook.
other_parameter_results.ai_provenance: AlphaEvolve used code for generating Singer difference sets supplied by human researchers; the paper describes this result as an AI-assisted improvement.
other_parameter_results.reproduction_status: Not the fixed N=6166 configuration and not used as this task's best value.

optimality_status.analytic_lower_bound: Banakh and Gavrylkiv (2017), Theorem 4.1: lim Delta(n)^2/n = inf Delta(n)^2/n >= 2 + max_{0<phi<pi} 2 sin(phi)/(phi+pi). At phi=pi/2 this is >= 2+4/(3*pi) > 80/33 because pi<22/7. Therefore 33*Delta(6166)^2 > 80*6166 = 493280. Since 122^2*33=491172<493280 and 123^2*33=499257>493280, Delta(6166)>=123.
optimality_status.counting_lower_bound: The simpler pair-count bound is k(k-1)/2 >= 6166 and implies k >= 112; the analytic lower bound 123 is stronger.
optimality_status.upper_bound: An exact 128-mark witness is saved and checked.
optimality_status.limitation: No exact value was found in the checked paper, cited classical sources, or current AlphaEvolve problem repository. This is a bounded source survey, not a proof that no later result exists.

alphaevolve_paper.claims: Defines Delta(n) using integer differences; reports the prior 128^2/6166 upper bound and a later AlphaEvolve improvement at N=49109.

cyclic_difference_bases_paper.sections: §3.1 Singer's theorem; §4.1 Leech-Golay bounds; Table 3 lists N=6166 and 128 marks.

alphaevolve_repository.scope: The notebook gives the 49109-parameter evolved construction and is not the 6166/128 historical witness.

human_baseline_source.proof_source: Saarela and Vanhatalo, A Connection Between Unbordered Partial Words and Sparse Rulers, EJC 33(1) (2026), #P1.40, https://doi.org/10.37236/13806

limitations: The finite optimum at N=6166 is not established; 128 is a feasible upper bound only.
The reconstructed 128-mark witness is not claimed to be the identical historical Leech or Golay witness.
The AlphaEvolve improvement at N=49109 is kept separate from the fixed N=6166 task.
The task accepts unrestricted integer marks and must not be reinterpreted as a sparse ruler of length 6166.

frozen_human_baseline.source: Wichmann (1963), reconstructed as W(38,3); completeness formula and proof in Saarela and Vanhatalo (2026), Definitions 8 and 16 and Theorem 18.
frozen_human_baseline.evidence_state: The 158-mark Wichmann construction has length 6548 and is exactly checked for every required distance 1..6166. This weaker baseline is distinct from the source-reported best human record of 128.
frozen_human_baseline.origin_type: published human construction; restricted ruler is a feasible unrestricted integer difference basis

details.ambient_group: integers_under_subtraction; differences larger than N are allowed
